title: Tax exempted and tax handed back, from the City’s own books
question: What do the City’s annual financial reports show for property value exempted from tax, and for property tax returned after it was collected?
finding: The City’s financial report puts exemptions that the State does not repay at $22.32 billion of assessed value in fiscal 2025, 6.0% of all assessed value, up from $8.25 billion (4.1%) in fiscal 2016: about $223.2 million a year at the 1% basic rate, against $82.5 million. Separately, collections on earlier years’ property tax turned negative: the report shows net givebacks of $12.9 million for the fiscal 2023 levy; $35.6 million for the fiscal 2024 levy; $87.3 million for the fiscal 2025 levy, which it attributes to exemptions being applied to earlier years and to Assessment Appeals Board decisions that offices, hotels and retail property had been over-assessed. The Board also approved 96 settlements of tax-refund claims from fiscal 2016 to 2025, $170.8 million in all.
how: From the statistical tables of the Controller’s Annual Comprehensive Financial Reports: “Assessed Value of Taxable Property” (the non-reimbursable exemptions column and the reimbursable homeowners’ column) and “Property Tax Levies and Collections” (the column “collections in subsequent years”, which the report says nets redemptions against reductions of earlier years’ tax). Each year’s figure is taken from the latest report that prints it; the reports print thousands of dollars. Tax at 1% is the exempt value times the basic rate stated in the same table’s notes. Settlement counts are Board files titled as settlements whose text speaks of a tax refund or overpayment, by the fiscal year passed.
limits: An exemption is the law working: the report itself traces these to the State Constitution, and a refund after a successful assessment appeal returns money the owner should not have been billed. The exemption figure here is wider than the roll’s institutional exemptions in the previous screens (the report counts all assessed property and every exemption the State does not repay; the roll screens count the institutional codes on the secured roll), so the two do not match and should not be added. A negative figure for later collections is a net number: it does not say how many owners were refunded or how much each. The tables read here give no figure for refunds by taxpayer or by kind of tax. What would supply that: the Assessment Appeals Board’s decisions and the Treasurer and Tax Collector’s record of refunds. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
